analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and the `stop` row in the sampling-parameter table (line 2122). The row now says Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers exclude reasoning and tool-call spans per request through `ReasoningStopScope`, and that the native block engine matches the whole output with no scope. I examined both supplied head-text excerpts (lines 2835-3590). They are unchanged context describing the cluster, Flint, cache and link-probe documentation. No source code, key custody, attestation, wire protocol, authorization or cache-storage behavior is modified.

The stop-scope documentation concerns output post-processing of stop strings, a provider-side behavior. It does not touch T-041 (prefix-cache storage, scope or TTL), the coordinator-provider encryption boundary (TB-002), or the attestation and App Attest boundaries (TB-009, TB-011). It makes no new security claims and weakens no stated invariant. The excerpts mention prefix-cache tenant partitions, the add-on hold and the cluster worker boundary only as unchanged text, with no new attack surface.

Remaining question for integration: the new documentation asserts code behavior (`ReasoningStopScope`, `EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift`) that this batch cannot verify. That is a documentation-accuracy matter and not a security regression. I found no evidence that threat-model assumptions are invalidated.
